steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a quick, 60-second rundown of the main differences between DNA and RNA:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (missing one oxygen)  
   • RNA contains ribose  

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA uses A, T, C, G  
   • RNA uses A, U (uracil), C, G  

3. Strandedness  
   • DNA is usually double-stranded (double helix)  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded  

4. Location & stability  
   • DNA resides mainly in the nucleus (very stable)  
   • RNA travels to the cytoplasm (less stable, short-lived)  

5. Primary roles  
   • DNA stores and transmits genetic information across generations  
   • RNA plays diverse roles in protein synthesis (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) and regulation  

In short: DNA is the long-term genetic blueprint; RNA is the versatile working copy used to build and regulate proteins.
